thesis_check_315_blocker.claim: 315's blocker (Zgliczynski's dissipative/parabolic hypotheses vs BCG's quasilinear hyperbolic system) does NOT transfer to route 4's object
thesis_check_315_blocker.verdict: CONFIRMED, adjudicated (not merely carried) by this leg
thesis_check_315_blocker.reasoning: The self-similar/dynamically-rescaled 3D Navier-Stokes system (leg 260/253's object) is obtained from u(x,t)=(2(T-t))^{-1/2} V(y,s) and retains the viscous term as a Laplacian in the rescaled variable (nu * Delta_y V), i.e. its principal part is elliptic/parabolic and dissipative, plus a linear drift term -(y.grad V)/2 - V and the quadratic nonlinearity -(V.grad)V - grad P. This is the textbook rescaled-NS system whose hypotheses Necas-Ruzicka-Sverak (1996) and Tsai (1998) state theorems for (pinned at leg_253.md:30-31, parked, read-only here). BCG's compressible-Euler imploding profile (route 4's O1 in leg 315) has NO diffusive term at all -- viscosity/dissipation enters only as an exponentially-decaying forcing prefactor e^{-delta_dis s0} (leg_315.md:73, quoted verbatim below), which is why leg 315 classed the ODE-to-PDE bridge as blocked on a PDE-type mismatch. Route 4's actual object does not have that mismatch: it is genuinely parabolic/dissipative in its principal part, matching Zgliczynski's stated hypothesis class (math/0005247 abstract: 'topological method for the study of the dynamics of dissipative PDEs').
thesis_check_315_blocker.leg_315_quote_verbatim: the bridge from validated ODE to validated PDE is Zgliczynski's self-consistent a-priori bounds (math/0005247), whose hypotheses are dissipative. BCG's rescaled system is quasilinear hyperbolic with dissipation as an e^{-delta_dis s0}-decaying forcing. That mismatch is a theorem nobody has proved, not a package nobody installed.

obstruction_named.statement: Every located realization of the self-consistent-a-priori-bounds / Galerkin-plus-tail / NK-in-Fourier-space periodic-orbit-or-branch certification technology closes its tail-domination (neglected-mode) estimate against a COMPACT domain (periodic torus, bounded box with Dirichlet/Navier BC, or minimal periodic cell) with a discrete, geometrically/exponentially decaying Fourier or Chebyshev spectral basis. Route 4's object requires the opposite: an UNBOUNDED domain (R^3) carrying an ALGEBRAICALLY weighted space (leg 260: L^p(p>3) or weighted L^2(rho), s>1), explicitly excluding the one weight family (Gaussian, exponentially/super-geometrically decaying) that would supply an analogous discrete, rapidly-decaying spectral basis. No located instance of the technology has closed a tail-domination estimate against an algebraic (non-exponential) far field for a time-periodic target, in more than 1D, or with a Leray projector.
risk_factors_flagged_not_proven_fatal: leg_334.md section 3.3 (writeup/data/p2_route_dssp_v1.json, this repository's own model) measured that in the algebraically-weighted space, the linearization has CONTINUOUS spectrum, vs. discrete spectrum in the (wrong, excluded) Gaussian weight -- flagged as a risk factor for building a matched Galerkin-tail closure, NOT transferred as a proof of failure, because leg 334's finding is about the LINEARIZED STABILITY operator of a specific candidate in Route-E's model, a different specific operator from 'does a Galerkin-truncation basis exist for the state space', and conflating the two would overclaim

leg 341 (Route-ALGW) found three independent realizations of an algebraic-weight CAP apparatus already died, for three different mechanisms, for the STATIONARY-profile/NK problem (S1_A sup-norm collocation Z1>=6.0424, S1_B ell^1_w no window at any exponent, S1_C origin-H^2/Mellin a=0-only) -- named as a suggestive but NOT direct precedent, since the apparatus in leg 341 (NK fixed-point contraction) differs from the apparatus this leg scopes (Galerkin-plus-tail dynamical closure via Conley index or covering relations)

cost_class.reasoning: Research-level: no located instance of the technology has been built or evidenced against an unbounded, algebraically-weighted domain for a periodic-orbit target; the one located unbounded+algebraic-decay rigorous result (Hou-Luo, arXiv:2308.01528) is a different apparatus (analytic fixed point, not Galerkin-tail) for a different object kind (stationary, 1D). This mirrors leg 315's own cost-classing reasoning for its O1 (also class C): 'that mismatch is a theorem nobody has proved, not a package nobody installed' -- here the analogous statement is 'no located instance is a construction nobody has attempted in this exact combination, not a package nobody installed'.
cost_class.not_class_A_because: no pip-installable / off-the-shelf periodic-orbit CAP tool targets unbounded algebraically-weighted domains (none searched for or found this leg; consistent with capabilities.py's own live grep at leg 334: 0 periodic-orbit modules, 0 3D velocity fields, 0 Leray projections in this repository)
cost_class.not_class_B_because: the gap is not merely an un-hand-rolled implementation of a known closed-form estimate -- the tail-domination estimate itself (the mathematical content that lets a Galerkin truncation be justified) has no located precedent in this domain/weight combination; building it would be new mathematics, matching leg 315's own A/B/C rubric for O1

no_definite_c3_claim: This leg does NOT claim a proof that the Galerkin-tail bridge CANNOT close in the algebraic-weight setting (that would be classification iii, DOES-NOT-REACH, and would require a named failing hypothesis established as a fact, not an absence-of-evidence). No such failing hypothesis was located or derived this leg; the continuous-spectrum flag above is a risk factor about a different specific operator, not a proof about the Galerkin-truncation-basis question. Classification (ii) is chosen because a real, positively-identified domain-shape gap exists (named above) and is cost-classed, not because impossibility was shown.
